newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Iberia, Venezuela fund reach Viasa deal.
newsitem.headline: Iberia, Venezuela fund reach Viasa deal.

text.p: A preliminary agreement to save Venezuelan airline Viasa from bankruptcy was reached on Tuesday, the state-run National Investment Fund (FIV) said.

The fund said in a statement that the agreement was worked out in Madrid during talks between FIV President Alberto Poletto and representatives of Spain's national carrier Iberia, which holds the largest stake in Viasa with 45 percent.
The deal still must be accepted by the airline's 2,200 employees.
The FIV statement provided no specific figures.
Viasa grounded its aircraft on January 23 after the workers rejected an emergency cost-cutting plan earlier this month.
Venezuela, through the FIV, holds a 40 percent share in Viasa, and the country's largest bank, Banco Provincial, owns 15 percent.
Viasa recorded a $30 million loss last year and has not reported a profit since Iberia took over its management in 1991.
